payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_spec_review.py::test_a_spec_review_routes_on_the_severities_in_its_last_json_block stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/spec_review.py. The claim was "`read_spec_review` reads the last fenced `json` block of a `SpecReviewSession`'s text and carries its cost and `resets_at`. A block opens with a line that is ```` ```json ```` and closes at the next line that holds only ```` ``` ````. It keeps each finding's `fixes`. `spec_review_route` routes a read with `resets_at` set `wait`, before any other check. It routes the read `error` when the session carries an error, when the text holds no `json` block, or when that block is not an object whose `findings` is a list of objects. It routes `error` too when a finding has no string `claim`, a `severity` other than `blocker`, `concern` or `note`, or a `fixes` other than an entry of `SPEC_REVIEW_TAGS`, null or absent. `SPEC_REVIEW_TAGS` is the tuple `scope`, `build`, `witness`, and the read looks it up when called. Otherwise one `blocker` or more routes `escalate`, whatever its `fixes`, and none routes `run`. A `concern` whose `fixes` is `witness` routes `run` and keeps that `fixes`. Other keys are ignored. The witness drives each member, and a tag added to `SPEC_REVIEW_TAGS`.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
